title: Renewal Rescue: Action Matrix & Exec Escalation Kit
body:
Purpose:
This working doc is a practical, lightweight kit for identifying at-risk renewals, staging targeted mitigation plays, and escalating to executives when needed. It combines a risk scoring rubric, a fast-action play matrix, escalation templates (email + meeting brief), and a renewal-tracker column spec to standardize handoffs across CS, AE, solutions, and exec sponsors. Designed to be used in QBR prep and day-to-day triage.

Scope and intended users:
- Primary: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Renewal AEs, Solutions Engineers
- Secondary: Customer Success Operations, Sales Leadership, Product Manager on call
- Not covered: legal/contract negotiations beyond standard concession thresholds (see escalation rules)

1) Quick risk signals (automatic + manual)
Use these signals as inputs to the score below. Flag a case for immediate triage if any red (hard) triggers occur.
Hard triggers (immediate):
- Contract value at stake > $100k and any of: 30%+ drop in monthly API token usage vs trailing 3-month avg; unaddressed Sev1/Sev2 support incident in last 7 days; security/compliance objection unresolved after 10 business days.
- Customer publicly announces a competing vendor pilot that impacts core workflow.
Soft signals (weightable):
- Engagement: decline in active seats or seats not used > 25% in past 60 days.
- Health: unresolved feature gap noted in 2+ meetings or repeated quality regressions found in evals.
- Commercial: delayed PO or procurement > 30 days past expected renewal commit.
- Sentiment: negative CSAT/NPS follow-up or escalating tone in account threads.

2) Renewal risk score (0-100) - sample rubric
Scoring guidance: map signals into buckets and produce a single 0-100 score. Use thresholds to pick plays and whether to escalate.
- Usage change (0-30): +20 if drop >=30%, +10 if drop 15-30%, 0 if stable or growth.
- Severity of incidents (0-20): +20 if Sev1 in last 30d, +10 if repeated Sev2, +0 otherwise.
- Commercial friction (0-20): +20 if PO delayed >30d or legal redlines pending, +10 if pricing dispute in negotiation.
- Executive engagement (0-15): +15 if exec sponsor inactive >60d, +8 if sporadic.
- Product fit signals (0-15): +15 if fundamental gap identified, +8 if workarounds cause 25%+ dev overhead.
Interpretation: 0-25 = green, 26-55 = amber, 56-100 = red.

3) Action matrix (risk x time till renewal)
Columns: Risk band | Time to renewal | Primary owner | Immediate plays (0-7d) | 7-30d plays | 30-90d plays | Escalation required?
Example rows (abbreviated):
- Green | >90d | CSM | Monitor, schedule QBR prep \u2013 prep impact stories | Maintain cadence, optimize ARR growth motions | Plan expansion plays | No
- Amber | 30-90d | CSM + AE | Rapid technical health check, usage deep-dive, targeted enablement session | Offer custom success milestones, commercial sweetener up to 5% discount (CS ops pre-authorized) | Escalation to Solutions Eng for prioritized roadmap ask, pilot quantifiable outcome | Maybe, if score trending up
- Red | <90d | CSM + AE + Head of CS | Lock exec touchpoint within 48h, deploy \"rescue sprint\" (SE pairing, prioritized bugfix lane), pause auto-renew if needed | Immediate commercial concession templated, propose time-limited pilot at reduced rate, assign exec sponsor | Emergency contract ladder: involve Legal+Revenue leadership for >10% concessions; prepare churn contingency plan | Yes, escalate to CRO and Head of Product for roadmap commitments

4) Escalation ladder and criteria
- Level 1 (CS Leadership)
  - Trigger: score >=56 OR single hard trigger met for accounts <$250k ARR.
  - Action: 24-48h leader review, defined 7-day rescue plan, assign accountable owner.
- Level 2 (Sales Revenue Leader + Solutions Eng Director)
  - Trigger: Score >=70 OR any hard trigger for accounts >=$250k ARR OR renewal <45 days.
  - Action: 48h exec touch, potential commercial concession up to 10% (pre-approved), priority product bug/feature slot.
- Level 3 (CRO/Head of Product + Legal)
  - Trigger: Score >=85 OR imminent churn for >$500k ARR OR breach of SLA with business/financial impact.
  - Action: Formal executive commitment, legal exceptions, cross-org war room.

5) Templates (copy-paste friendly snippets)
A) Exec escalation email subject line:
  \"Urgent: Renewal at Risk \u2014 [Account] (Score: [XX]) \u2014 Request for exec touch\"
Body (short):
  - One-line problem statement
  - Key metrics (usage delta, open Sev incidents, days to renewal)
  - Primary ask (exec intro / product prioritization / commercial oversight)
  - Proposed next step and timing

B) Customer outreach opener (CSM -> Champion, for amber/red):
  \"Hi [Name], noticed recent drop in [feature] usage and want to make sure were aligned on next steps. Can we do a focused 30-minute health check this week? Ive already pulled usage metrics and have a proposed quick-win plan to restore value.

6) Renewal tracker column spec (single-source-of-truth for CS ops)
Required columns (for each account row):
- account_id, account_name, ARR, renewal_date, days_to_renewal, renewal_owner, risk_score, risk_band, primary_champion, exec_sponsor, last_usage_delta_pct, open_sev_count, legal_status, commercial_offer (Y/N), last_touch_date, next_action, escalation_level, notes_link
Operational notes: populate risk_score weekly from automated pipeline; CSM updates "next_action" after each engagement; Owner must set "escalation_level" when score crosses thresholds.

7) Sample 7-day rescue sprint checklist (what to do first 7 days for a red account)
Day 0-1: Triage meeting (CSM, AE, SE), assemble playbook, lock exec availability.
Day 1-3: SE-led technical deep-dive, prioritized list of blockers, triage tickets to engineering with SLOs.
Day 3-5: Customer success-led adoption work (onboarding, focused enablement), deploy quick fixes and measure delta.
Day 5-7: Review outcomes with customer and exec sponsor; agree measurable renewal criteria and commercial path.

8) Commercial concession guardrails
- Pre-authorized concessions (no legal): credits up to 5% of ARR or one-time $25k credit, whichever smaller, for accounts < $250k ARR.
- Require Sales Ops + Legal for concessions >5% or multi-year payment schedule exceptions.
- Always document concession rationale in renewal tracker and attach approval ticket.

9) QBR talking guide (focused, 20-minute slot oriented to renewals)
- 0-3m: Framing & current health snapshot (score, usage trend, top support items)
- 3-8m: Value recap (ROI/kpis customer cares about, case studies within account)
- 8-14m: Roadmap & mitigations (what were shipping that matters to them; dates)
- 14-18m: Commercial posture (timelines, optional concessions, path to expansion)
- 18-20m: Decision & next steps (explicit ask for renewal next step)

10) Measurement and post-mortem
- Immediate KPIs to track after play activation: usage delta (7/30/90d), open Sev counts, time to first value post-play, customer sentiment (CSAT).
- Post-renewal retrospective template: what triggered risk, what worked, what didnt, improvements (owner + due date). Capture in monthly "rescue retrospective" doc.

11) Escalation play examples (real short scripts)
- Product prioritization ask (to Head of Product): \"Customer [X] is at risk (score 78). They require a small roadmap commitment to ship feature Y by [date]. If not prioritized, likely loss of [ARR]. Request 2-week priority slot or documented alternative.\"
- Exec call request (to CRO): \"Request 30-min call between CRO and CEO of [Customer]. Primary ask: discuss path to fulfilling business outcome and remove procurement/legal blockers.\"

12) Quick wins library (library of low-friction items CSMs can run in 72h)
- Temporary API parameter tweak that improves latency for critical path (config change).
- Sandbox import of customer data to demonstrate new capability with sample dataset.
- Pre-built prompt templates and eval runner to quickly improve model outputs for their use case.

13) Runbook (how to activate this doc in practice)
- Step 1: Run risk scoring job and triage accounts weekly in CS ops meeting.
- Step 2: For any account scoring >56, create a rescue ticket and populate tracker columns.
- Step 3: Assign owners and set 48h checkpoint. Escalate to Level 1 if no measurable progress.
- Step 4: Capture all customer-facing concessions in ticketing system and attach approval IDs.

Appendices (links and examples)
- Example renewal tracker CSV header (copy into Sheets).
- Full email templates and exec briefing slide template (linked artifacts above).

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Define exact thresholds for pre-authorized concession percentages by ARR band (ops to propose).
- Build automated signal that flags public competitor pilot mentions (marketing/ops to own).
- Decide retention bonus guidelines for AEs when a deal is saved (revenue comp policy).

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally prescriptive and built for rapid operationalization. We expect the rubric and guardrails to be adjusted after 3 months of running live rescues. Please add recommended edits inline and link sample accounts where this should be piloted (suggest 8-12 accounts across ARR tiers).
